--- Page 1 (Beckerman_45a) --- Dear Folks: I haven't heard from you during the past week. By the time you receive this letter I think Ruth will be home. I would like Mamma to keep writing her own letters because they are very easy to read and understand. We are all still waiting for the latest news about discharges. I can not tell you anything definite about the future but I think that it should not take too long. During the past week Sam Schneider promised to see me and I am hoping to be home by Christmas. --- Page 2 (Beckerman_45b) --- I am also looking forward to going home. May Handler has already left here. I haven't heard from Abe all week. Tried to call him the last few days but was unable to get in touch with him by phone. I am going to ride out to his quarters tomorrow and find out if he is still around. The last time I saw him he told me he may be leaving. I wrote you a short note the other day about my promotion. It was really good luck and was a big surprise to me. I would like you to ask Aunt Sarah for [illegible] heart. Jaado. I've n --- Page 3 (Beckerman_45c) --- a lot of Navy and also, [illegible] home or is he still in Europe. I wrote to the Naturalization Office and you will probably hear from them soon. Have you received any of the packages I sent from Australia? I sent some gifts to you in the early part of June. If you can, would you send me some film size 616, 120, or 127. My camera is out of order so don't send size 116. I remember you mentioning that you received a [illegible] war bond. Beginning with the month of March you should --- Page 4 (Beckerman_45d) --- 4 Receiving me every minute. The 37.50 price is deducted from my monthly pay. I am still in best of health and all is fine. Please write soon. The Jack
